gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: 20 original sentences covering completed actions, sequences, past habits, negatives, and questions — always with a clear finished-time marker, never a present-perfect one.

questions.explain: A finished action at a specific past time: last Saturday.
'Yesterday morning' — a clear, finished time in the past.
'Buy' is irregular: buy → bought.

questions.after: my umbrella on the train yesterday.
questions.explain: 'Leave' is irregular: leave → left.

questions.after: the meeting at the last minute last Friday.
questions.explain: Short verb ending in a single consonant: double it before -ed — cancelled.
One completed action after another: the film finished, then we walked home.

questions.before: He finished his homework, and then he
questions.explain: 'Then' links two completed actions, one after the other.
'Get' is irregular: get → got.

questions.before: When I was a child, I
questions.after: a bike to school every day.
questions.explain: A repeated habit that's now over — past simple, not present.

questions.after: football every weekend when we were kids.
questions.explain: 'Every weekend' describes a past routine, now finished.
A hobby she had when she was young — a past habit, now finished.

questions.after: in this town his whole life, until he died in 2010.
questions.explain: A finished past state: he lived here until his death, so use past simple.

questions.before: When I was a teenager, I
questions.after: hard for every test at school.
questions.explain: A past habit at a finished time ('when I was a teenager'). Consonant + y → change y to i before -ed: studied.
Negative past simple: didn't + base verb.
After 'didn't', the verb goes back to its base form: go, not went.
'Didn't' + base verb — never 'didn't finished'.

questions.after: the bus on Monday, so we walked.
questions.explain: Negative past simple with the base form: catch, not caught.
Past simple questions always start with 'did', whatever the subject.

questions.explain: 'Did' + subject + base verb — the main verb stays uninflected.

questions.after: he pass his driving test last week?

Wrong tense: "last year" is a finished time — use past simple, not present perfect.
Wrong tense: this describes one completed trip, not a scene in progress.

"Buy" is irregular: buy → bought, not buyed.
"Eat" is irregular: eat → ate, not eated.
"Think" is irregular: think → thought, not thinked.
"Bring" is irregular: bring → brought, not bringed.
Double the final consonant in a short CVC verb — "dropped", not "droped".
Consonant + y → change y to i before -ed — "copied", not "copyed".
Double the final consonant — "chatted", not "chated".
Consonant + y → change y to i before -ed — "tried", not "tryed".
Consonant + y → change y to i before -ed — "carried", not "carryed".
"Yesterday" is a finished time — this needs past simple, not present simple.
"Last night" is a finished time — this needs past simple, not present simple.
A specific past year needs past simple, not present simple.
"Two days ago" is a finished time — this needs past simple, not present simple.
"Last summer" is a finished time — this needs past simple, not present simple.
After "didn't", the verb goes back to its base form — "go", not "went".
After "didn't", use the base form — "see", not "saw".
After "did", the main verb stays in its base form — "go", not "went".
Wrong tense: the past negative is "didn't", not "don't".
Wrong tense: the past negative is "didn't", not "doesn't".
